Contact benchmark · 3D replays

Archived detailed-CAD thin-object pilots

Load a preview to explore saved states. Drag to orbit, right-drag to pan, and scroll to zoom. One 3D case is active at a time; plots stay visible. All panes show convex scene colliders; IPC’s solver uses triangle surfaces.

Some test cases have two sets of simulation parameters per backend: General is each backend’s baseline preset, used across all cases. Tuned uses higher iteration budgets for the wedge cases. For thin objects, MJWarp uses stiffer contact regularization and more substeps, IPC uses a smaller barrier distance, and Steel uses more substeps. Geometry, mass, friction coefficients and drive settings stay fixed. Exact parameters are folded below each case.

Timing hardware: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Laptop GPU (8188 MiB VRAM), NVIDIA driver 580.178.04. Host: Linux-6.8.0-45-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.39, 32 logical CPUs.

Timing setup: one environment on GPU (CUDA), at 240 Hz. Each timed frame includes all physics substeps and GPU completion synchronization. Rendering, recording, control updates, state readback, setup, warm-up and compilation are excluded.

Linear shake

A YAM Linear 4310 gripper grasps and lifts a cube (m = 0.05 kg) using PD-controlled jaws with a constant drive-force limit of 12 N per jaw, then performs 3 s of linear shaking.

Thin object pick and shake

A YAM Linear 4310 gripper closes on a 4 × 2 × 20 mm steel coupon (m = 1.248 g) in 0.2 s, lifts it 80 mm, then shakes it horizontally with the cube test’s 20 mm amplitude and 2 Hz frequency for 3 s (0.5 s ramps). Shared PD-controlled jaws have a 2 N drive-force limit per jaw. Every backend uses the same simplified symmetric approximation of the stock fingers.

BackendParam VariantRetainedMax slip (mm)Physics (ms/frame)
PhysXGeneralYes0.0134.095
MJWarpGeneralYes1.0391.375
MJWarpTunedYes0.1075.232
IPCGeneralYes0.00177.706
IPCTunedYes0.00174.715
Newton (Steel)GeneralNo92.3260.551
Newton (Steel)TunedYes0.0139.555

Slip is object displacement in the actual gripper frame, measured from the end of closing through raised hold, shake and post-hold (4.7–9.7 s). The shaded interval is shaking (5.7–8.7 s). Theoretical GT is ideal sticking at zero; an analytical impact trajectory is not asserted. Retained requires at least 60 mm of rise throughout hold, shake and post-hold.

MJWarp tuning: Tuned uses a 1 ms contact time constant, 16 physics substeps and a 100-step line-search budget. This jointly refines soft-contact regularization and time resolution; friction coefficients, geometry and PD drives are unchanged. Measured preload is about 1.48 N/jaw in General and 2 N/jaw in Tuned.

IPC tuning: Tuned changes only the barrier distance, from 0.5 mm to 0.05 mm. Its timestep, friction smoothing and solver tolerances stay fixed. The same preset is validated on both thin-object motions.

Steel tuning: General uses 12 iterations and one physics step per control frame. Tuned keeps 12 iterations and uses 16 collision/dynamics substeps (3840 Hz physics, 240 Hz control), with the same scene, shake and drives. This preset was selected in the earlier static thin-capture/release study; the viewers, curves and table above are fresh pick-and-shake measurements. Increasing iterations alone did not rescue static capture in that earlier study.

Timing: dedicated synchronized GPU physics only, three episodes per variant (IPC: one), including every substep. Replay is downsampled; curves and errors use the original 240 Hz measurements. Measurements · Steel tuning data.

Thin object rocking

A YAM Linear 4310 gripper closes on a 4 × 2 × 20 mm steel coupon (m = 1.248 g) in 0.2 s, lifts it 80 mm, then rocks it about the grasp point using the cube test’s ±12° roll and pitch at 1.5 Hz, with a 90° phase offset, for 3 s (0.5 s ramps). There is no commanded translation during rocking. Shared PD-controlled jaws have a 2 N drive-force limit per jaw. Every backend uses the same simplified symmetric approximation of the stock fingers.

BackendParam VariantRetainedMax slip (mm)Physics (ms/frame)
PhysXGeneralYes0.0153.930
MJWarpGeneralYes7.4851.550
MJWarpTunedYes0.4245.520
IPCGeneralYes0.56886.125
IPCTunedYes0.00185.035
Newton (Steel)GeneralNo91.8300.549
Newton (Steel)TunedYes0.0129.525

Slip is object displacement in the actual gripper frame, measured from the end of closing through raised hold, shake and post-hold (4.7–9.7 s). The shaded interval is rocking (5.7–8.7 s). The gripper frame follows its measured rotation. Theoretical GT is ideal sticking at zero; an analytical impact trajectory is not asserted. Retained requires at least 60 mm of rise throughout hold, shake and post-hold.

MJWarp tuning: Tuned uses a 1 ms contact time constant, 16 physics substeps and a 100-step line-search budget. This jointly refines soft-contact regularization and time resolution; friction coefficients, geometry and PD drives are unchanged. Measured preload is about 1.48 N/jaw in General and 2 N/jaw in Tuned.

IPC tuning: Tuned changes only the barrier distance, from 0.5 mm to 0.05 mm. Its timestep, friction smoothing and solver tolerances stay fixed. In rocking, this reduces max slip from 0.568 mm to 0.00138 mm. The smaller stand-off limits the rotation-dependent drift seen with General’s finite contact gap.

Steel tuning: General uses 12 iterations and one physics step per control frame. Tuned keeps 12 iterations and uses 16 collision/dynamics substeps (3840 Hz physics, 240 Hz control), with the same scene, shake and drives. This preset was selected in the earlier static thin-capture/release study; the viewers, curves and table above are fresh pick-and-shake measurements. Increasing iterations alone did not rescue static capture in that earlier study.

Timing: dedicated synchronized GPU physics only, three episodes per variant (IPC: one), including every substep. Replay is downsampled; curves and errors use the original 240 Hz measurements. Measurements · Steel tuning data.

Snap wedge (horizontal + table friction)

A YAM Linear 4310 gripper squeezes a wedge (m = 0.15 kg) on the table using PD-controlled jaws. The per-jaw drive-force limit ramps linearly from 1 to 12 N between 5 and 11 s.

PhysXTuned1.0685.530
MJWarpGeneral0.9461.472
IPCGeneral0.21344.859
Newton (Steel)General2.0790.585
Newton (Steel)Tuned0.6711.526

Error: absolute per-jaw force-limit difference at the first saved 0.5 mm forward motion; theoretical onset = 4.362 N/jaw. Speed: median dedicated physics timing, 240 Hz frames.

Forward world-X displacement from the closed pose at 4.6 s; the plot covers the 5–11 s force ramp. Solid: general; dashed: tuned. Theoretical GT reuses the full report’s finite-geometry Coulomb model, including capped PD drives, jaw clearance and table-friction braking. It assumes a fixed gripper and no wedge rotation.

Snap wedge (vertical)

A horizontal YAM Linear 4310 gripper approaches from the side and lifts an upward-widening wedge (m = 0.15 kg, 45° faces, μ = 0.8) at 1 N/jaw, holds, then ramps the drive-force limit to 12 N/jaw between 6.5 and 9.5 s. The wedge sits at the table edge, clear of the finger openings. At the settled 22.4° pitch, the ideal fixed-pitch holding window is 0.149–6.049 N/jaw.

BackendParam VariantOnset error (N/jaw)Physics (ms/frame)
PhysXGeneral3.6643.405
PhysXTuned3.9085.400
MJWarpGeneral0.0581.371
IPCGeneral0.11978.947
Newton (Steel)General0.3640.567
Newton (Steel)Tuned0.1191.438

Error: absolute per-jaw force-limit difference at the first saved (60 Hz) 0.5 mm upward slip after hold; tilted-model onset = 6.375 N/jaw. No pickup means the initial lift/hold failed. Speed: median dedicated physics timing, 240 Hz frames.

Positive displacement is upward world-Z motion relative to the gripper, zeroed at the end of hold. Solid: General; dashed: Tuned. Theory starts from the settled pre-ramp CPU pose (22.4°), uses 3D Coulomb friction, moving-finger inertia and capped PD drives, and follows sliding beyond onset. It ends at 16.75 mm at the symmetric model’s torque-support limit. This is a model validity limit; subsequent tumbling and table impacts are not predicted. No post-ramp trajectories are fitted.
